scientific_question: Are source-coobserved species contrasts in NIGHT-DAY observed GPS displacement associated with astronomical daylength only across different calendar months, or do relationships also persist within fixed calendar-year × month blocks of the SAME original study-shared days?
source_integrity: Before opening new within-month coefficients: verify original published Movebank source bitstream UUID/bytes/MD5 and each previously frozen native source q/daylength effect and original same-calendar date count/month block count, exactly the same first individual/date support, and the previously archived unadjusted daily taxon-difference photoperiod slopes to 1e-12. No source/taxon/day/month re-selection using q outcomes.
calendar_support: Same source study shared eligible (year, solar-local date) across all native taxa. Illinois: fixed point three-native common calendar, each source tag year >=10 source shared dates and reference 43N daylight variation >=0.5h. Wyoming: original 3 UTC sampling schedules each with the same source-tag supported dates as earlier Wyoming study; fixed-point two-native common calendar.
time_and_weather: Astronomical daylength at the SAME fixed 43 degrees north for both sources. No ERA5 weather is used. Date q difference computed per source-native species by equal available tagged animal daily q and subtracting second from first; retains source-native tag composition variation by day. Exact dates, GPS positions, year/month labels never emitted.
predefined_estimator: For each native species-pair q difference y_d and standardized 43N astronomical daylength L_d, for blocks b=(year,calendar_month), calculate centered x=L_d−mean_b L, centered y=y_d−mean_b y. Within-month coefficient beta=sum_b,d(x_center*y_center)/sum_b,d(x_center^2). This is ordinary OLS slope with block fixed intercepts, not independent astronomical/causal identification.
source_support: Eligible block >=5 shared dates, daylight span >=0.05h; eligible source >=5 eligible blocks, >=40 total days and sum within-block centered L² >=0.25 h². Thresholds frozen before new slope reading. No absence-to-zero conversion.
uncertainty: 2000 deterministic year-month BLOCK bootstrap resamples with replacement of eligible blocks; recompute within-block centered cross-products and slope, retaining block lengths. 2.5/97.5 percentile only if >=1900 finite bootstrap draws. Leave-one-month-block-out slope range. No iid GPS/day-level P values, nominal not multiple-comparison corrected.
result_scope: Two original studies, Illinois 3 taxon pairs and Wyoming one native taxon pair × 3 source GPS sampling schedules = six contrasts; represent only two independent field studies, not six independent populations or worldwide species guild effects. Preserve all four pairs and schedule statuses.
interpretation_ceiling: Within month/year fixed effects remove comparisons BETWEEN months but do not isolate photoperiod causality: astronomical L is a deterministic smooth function of calendar day and within-month date trends can proxy food, migration, breeding, temperature, wind, rainfall or observation effort.
Only nine source year-month blocks in Illinois and eight in Wyoming; block bootstrap intervals can be sensitive to cluster leverage and cannot be interpreted as global population confidence.

Different coobserved species may have changing original tagged animal composition, source detection frequencies, seasonal coverage, actual within-day GPS fix times and microhabitats despite SAME source calendar dates.
NIGHT−DAY q is observed log1p straight-line minimum GPS displacement speed not fraction of time active, energetic expenditure, prey capture or causal partitioning of true activity.
Original Illinois source pairs and their datewise q~daylength signs are already known; this is post-result diagnostic, not blind replication.
All old original source provider data and 48-source negative signed shortwave external nonreplication and 12 ERA5 JSON SHA historical HOLDS remain unchanged.
No original precise source year/month, individual tag ID, event date/time, GPS coordinate, per-tag speed or raw original telemetry is published.
